Episode #5: Magic Vision Promotion Committee
"I've put up with this long enough, but I've reached my limit. There's absolutely nothing interesting here. If the genre tropes alone are enough to satisfy you, be my guest. Adieu."

[Not even remotely entertaining. What exactly am I supposed to be watching this for? There's just an absurdly overpowered little girl and her maid, who's inexplicably obsessed with mastering martial arts. They effortlessly overpower everyone in sight, while a bunch of young noble girls get together, chatter away, and scheme about one thing or another.

Cute little girls, martial arts, overpowered characters, smug displays of superiority, a school setting... If those ingredients alone are enough to entertain you, then by all means, enjoy. I certainly can't.

Do I regret ranking the first episode at number one? Well... yes. Yes, I do.]

review.en:
Episode #5

Episode #5ː Conflict
"Is 'Conflict' supposed to refer to the inner turmoil of viewers who've somehow made it through five episodes of this show? I haven't been this utterly baffled since 'Magic Academy'..."

[The storytelling is an absolute disaster. What on earth is going on with the series composition? Noriko's feelings for Izark have suddenly skyrocketed, and she's somehow learned a whole lot of the language, too. Did I accidentally skip an episode or two? Apparently, quite a bit of time has passed, though the show does a terrible job of conveying it. And now they're hugging each other...?

Then Izark abruptly leaves Noriko without saying a word. Why? This sort of development is fairly typical of shojo manga, where the storytelling and presentation can somehow make it feel convincing. But simply reproducing it in anime without making the slightest effort to adapt how it's presented leaves viewers completely unable to follow what's happening.

After a string of outrageous incidents, Noriko suddenly gets harassed by some thugs, then somehow ends up falling and tumbling down onto a riverbank—or wherever that was. And wouldn't you know it, she just happens to run into a parent and child who've been instructed to look for her. Why a parent and child, anyway?

What the hell is this?? What is this show even trying to accomplish? It's astonishing how catastrophically bad the storytelling is.

Tomoyo Kurosawa... what on earth is happening here?]
review.jp:
第5話: ː 葛藤（かっとう）

"この作品を第5話まで見てしまっている視聴者の中の「葛藤」のこと?「魔法学園」以来の意味わかんねーよ…です"

絶望的な構成、シリーズ構成はどうなってる?1,2話くらい見忘れてた?って思うくらい唐突にノリコのイザークに対する想いは爆上がり、言葉も大分覚えてる…なんかよく分からない感じで時間が経過しているらしい。なんか抱き合ってるし・・・。で、唐突に何も言わずにイザークはノリコの元を去る。何故?こういったものは少女漫画特有で、マンガだとなんとなく納得の行く見せ方が出来るが、何の工夫も無くアニメでも同じ様に見せても誰も全くついてこれない。そして色々とんでもアプニングあってから、唐突に輩に絡まれるノリコ、そして河原?に落ちて転がってくるノリコ…。ノリコを探すように指示を受けていた親子（何故親子?）とたまたま出会う…。何だこれ??何がしたい?凄いなこれ、破滅的。黒沢ともよさん・・・何が起きている?

source_entries.synopsis:
Noriko Tachiki has dreamt of a beautiful fantasy land for some time, though her friends think it is only her imagination. One day, on her way home, Noriko stumbles upon a bomb disguised as a paper bag that explodes right in front of her. However, instead of dying, she is transported to a mysterious forest full of strange plants and creatures.

As she begins navigating through the woods, Noriko is suddenly attacked by a giant, worm-like monster. Fortunately, she is saved by Izark Kia Tarj, a swordsman who does not speak her language. Lacking the strength to survive on her own, Noriko decides to follow her stoic savior, taking the opportunity to learn the foreign land's language and be more useful to Izark.

Unbeknownst to her, Noriko is a crucial piece of an ancient prophecy. She is "The Awakening"—a being destined to unleash the greatest evil known as the "Sky Demon." With influential people plotting to capture Noriko for her supposed powers, both she and Izark must fend for themselves and overcome a future laced with chaos.

[Written by MAL Rewrite]
source_entries.synopsis_ja:
ごく普通の日々を送っていた女子高生・立木典子（たちき のりこ）は、ある朝見た不思議な夢に誘われるように、見知らぬ異世界へと迷い込んでしまう。言葉も常識も通用しないこの世界で、行く当てもなく彷徨う典子を救ったのは、たった一人で旅を続ける渡り戦士・イザークだった。
時を同じくして、世界中では「破壊をもたらす“天上鬼”を目覚めさせる者が現れる」「どの国よりも早く手に入れろ」と囁かれていた。目覚めとは、そして天上鬼とは何なのか——その答えを知るかのように、イザークは典子を見て呟く。
「この娘を殺さなければならない」言葉も文化も異なる二人の間には、それでも少しずつ小さな絆が芽生えていく。
そんな二人は、やがて壮大な運命の渦へと飲み込まれていく——。

weekly_intro.en: Fall 2026 anime has already entered its fifth week. Time really does fly. We're approaching the point where the early stretch begins to give way to the middle of the season, and we should be starting to see signs of the first little climaxes taking shape... Or at least, that's what I'd like to say. Unfortunately, aside from a handful of relatively big-name titles, so many of this season's crappy shows have been struggling to get anywhere since the very beginning. In fact, I'm not sensing anything resembling a midseason buildup, let alone even the slightest indication that they're laying the groundwork for something to come. What on earth is going on with this season? And where is it even heading from here? Those are the questions I keep asking myself. To make matters worse, several shows I've been keeping at least some interest in—Tetsuryo! Meet with Tetsudou Musume and #Searching for Zombies (and, well, PSYREN too, I suppose)—were off the air this week, making an already underwhelming week feel even more lackluster. Still, the season marches on, whether there's much to get excited about or not, and here we are, having made it through another week. Well then, with all that said, what exactly happened in the rankings this week? Let's take a closer look and see for ourselves.
weekly_intro.ja: ２０２６年秋アニメも早いもので第5週目に突入しました。 序盤から中盤戦もそろそろ架橋に入り、第一弾の小さな山場を迎えてくる兆しが見えてくる頃…と言いたいところですが、わずかながらな比較的ビッグタイトルは例外として、多くのク◯作品が序盤戦から伸び悩んでいたので、実のところ一切中盤の山場など感じない、ましてや種まきすらしている気配を感じえない今期となっています。一体どうなっているのでしょうか？そして今期、これからどうなるだろう？と思っているわけです。 また更に、そんな中でも個人的に多少気に留めている作品である、『てつりょー！meet with 鉄道むすめ』や、『＃ゾンビさがしてます』（あと一応『PSYREN -サイレン-』も）が今週は放送がお休みで、ますます盛り下がっていたわけです。とはいえ、それでもシーズンは淡々と進んでいくので、今週もこの日を無事迎えることが出来たわけなのです。 さぁて、そんなこんなですが、今週は一体どんな動きだったんでしょう。それでは実際にその中身をとくとご覧ください。

review.en:
Episode #18: (Total Ep. 18): Follow-up

"Every little piece comes together to create a quietly perfect portrayal of a child, a woman, and a mother. An absolute gem of an episode."

A perfect episode? At least for me, it was. The entire story unfolds through the inner monologue of a young elementary school girl who spends much of her time home alone. Her insecurities, her determination to be just a little better despite them, and her desire to cling to something like a lucky charm are all portrayed with remarkable sensitivity. Even her ordinary routine—spending time alone, listening to the evening radio, taking the train to and from cram school, and observing the people around her—never feels remotely boring. The little messages she repeatedly leaves for her mother also quietly reveal how thoughtful and sensible she is, always trying to be responsible and careful.

Then there's the incident involving people she encounters during those journeys, and the way the older woman hosting the radio program becomes involved. Without explicitly explaining anything, the episode also gives us enough to sense why this woman only accepts jobs involving children. And then comes the post-credits scene: the girl's radiant smile as she proudly shows off the uniform of the school she'd dreamed of attending, looking straight into her mother's camera. Meanwhile, the familiar voice of the radio host can be heard again, only now her program has moved from the evening to the morning—a new beginning. Every single piece falls perfectly into place.

Even the mother's love is conveyed so naturally, through the small detail that she postponed her night shifts for two months after the incident so she could accompany her daughter to and from cram school. And when you think about the girl's feelings as she finally pours out everything she'd been keeping bottled up, and those of the female assassin who listens to her so warmly—someone who presumably carries her own painful history involving children—it's genuinely hard to put the emotions into words. There isn't a single thing I could complain about. What a wonderful episode.

Episode #5: The Singing Crystal

"A surprisingly well-crafted series that reveals just how much thought and care goes into it when you pay attention. Far less shallow than its appearance might suggest."

This series may look rather plain, but it has a charm of its own. Despite its seemingly frivolous tone, the storytelling is actually quite thoughtful, and the direction feels surprisingly solid. It consistently leaves me with a good impression.

This time, Mimi and Elma go along with Hiro's outrageous plan, and the battle itself is given plenty of time and attention rather than being rushed through. What I particularly liked, though, was how the interactions immediately afterward—shopping, dealing with the guild, and responding to the military's invitation—subtly revealed the trust, affection, and growing intimacy between the three.

Even after they decide to make their escape, there's that conversation between the two girls during the hyperdrive journey, after Hiro has gone to bed. Elma casually tells Mimi, "It's your turn tonight, Mimi, so make sure you take a proper shower before going to Hiro." Little lines like that carry more meaning than they might seem to at first glance. The episode is full of these small but revealing details, and I really appreciated how naturally they're woven into the story.

review.en:
Episode #6: Oops!」「Ume and the Teacher」「Komaro's World

"Consistently entertaining throughout, with an outstanding final segment. I was also impressed by the show's willingness to take risks and challenge boundaries."

The tea ceremony club's bathroom situation was completely insane. I couldn't stop laughing... And the student council president getting her enormous breasts stuck while trying to climb out the window butt-first (naturally), leaving her in that utterly humiliating position, followed by her painfully desperate excuse, "I just wanted some fresh air..."—absolutely priceless. The beehive removal was handled pretty casually, but the pacing was great and it was surprisingly entertaining. And that teacher is seriously something else... Completely unhinged.

Up to that point, though, I was enjoying myself while thinking this would probably land somewhere in the mid-8s at best. Then came the final segment, "Komaro's World," and the way it tied back to that exchange just before the ending theme—"You're the only one Komaro is this attached to, Ume"—was brilliant. For several episodes now, I'd been wondering why Komaro was so inexplicably attached to Ume, and this provided a really satisfying payoff.

Something else struck me again this episode: this series casually throws in things that would normally be considered "absolutely outrageous—so outrageous that most creators wouldn't even dream of attempting them." And it deliberately refuses to react to those things as though they're inherently outrageous. In that sense, I'm beginning to see it as a challenge to today's increasingly excessive culture of finding fault with practically anything—particularly matters involving gender, sexual expression, and sexual preferences—and treating those objections as justification for attacking others. It also feels like a challenge to the pressures Japanese anime and manga are currently facing.

That defiant attitude made me want to support the series in my own way. Between that and how excellent the final segment was, I ended up giving this episode a 9.

review.en:
Episode #6: (Total Ep. #54): The Paper Village

"Things are taking a genuinely intriguing turn. There's still a lot of groundwork being laid and plenty we don't understand yet, but there's definitely something promising beginning to shine through."

Although the story is still very much in its groundwork-laying stage, it's gradually becoming more interesting. I particularly liked the circumstances that led Maomao to train another apothecary—someone who could eventually take over for her, or at least hold down the fort in her absence—and how that process was portrayed.

Meanwhile, Yabu somehow ends up accompanying Jinshi on a trip back to his hometown, supposedly for a vacation, for reasons that remain unclear. There's probably more going on behind the scenes, and it's still too early to figure out everyone's true intentions. Even so, I appreciated details like the way the farmers looked at the group as they passed by, as well as the beautiful stretches of green farmland and countryside. The portrayal of Yabu's character, particularly his compassion and concern for his family, was also well done.

As usual, Jinshi remains the only character I'm not entirely sold on. I imagine we'll eventually discover that the cat has some important significance, too. For an ordinary series, this would easily be a 9-point episode, but given the standards I hold this particular show to, unfortunately, it's an 8.

Episode #5

Episode #5ː I Don't Want to Stay Awkward /　Because I Don't Want It to Stay Awkward
"A little extra credit for featuring a train line I used to know well, but still a decent effort and a perfectly enjoyable, if fairly ordinary, episode."

[The Yokohama Seaside Line, a train line I used to be quite familiar with, played a major role this time, so I may have given the episode a little extra credit for that. Still, I enjoyed it well enough. There were some thoughtful touches, like using a boy who loves the line to cleverly introduce its various stations and distinctive features, including its rubber tires. I also appreciated how the episode resisted the temptation to make a big deal out of major local attractions, instead giving them only brief glimpses from a distance.

I'm not entirely convinced by how heavily the show leans on cuteness or how everything always seems to work out so smoothly, but I suppose that's part of its charm. The post-credits segment also did a nice job of introducing various local jobs and the people who do them, which left another positive impression. Nothing particularly remarkable overall, but a perfectly decent episode.]

review.en:
Episode #6: (Total Ep. #20): The School Festival

"An undeniably well-made series, but I'm getting tired of the endless coincidences and these circular journeys of emotional avoidance that end in self-satisfying resolutions."

The cultural festival... was surprisingly uneventful. It covered what it needed to, I suppose. Still, it felt strange that Yota and Koyun barely even spoke, considering how often they used to hang out, run into each other by chance, or walk home together. And has Miki completely lost interest in Minato now?

Then there's Koyun, thinking and overthinking everything all over again. Just as she seemingly managed to resolve her lingering feelings about her ex-boyfriend a couple of episodes ago, she now says something to Minato that will presumably help her clear up her complicated feelings toward him, too. It sounds reasonable enough on the surface, but isn't she really just going around in circles, finding convenient ways to make herself feel better without actually getting anywhere?

And of course, Momoka just happens to overhear their conversation... Seriously, enough with these coincidences already. I'm starting to get pretty tired of this whole pattern.

review.en:
Episode #6: So What's Wrong with Waging Wardrobe Warfare?

"Not bad at all. Far better than the previous episode's relentless fanservice. There are still some questionable aspects, but overall, it was surprisingly decent."

I wouldn't say there was anything particularly bad about this episode. The interactions with the prince, who possesses the absurdly overpowered ability to redo things, were interesting enough from a worldbuilding perspective, though that kind of ridiculous cheat ability also makes it hard to take the situation seriously. Still, it wasn't bad.

One thing that bothered me, though, was how obviously someone had moved upwind. Surely that should have prompted a little more thought or suspicion? It's the same frustration I often feel with stories where everything serves the plot first and foremost, and characters and events simply behave however they need to in order to deliver whatever the creators want to show us.

Nothing else particularly stood out as worthy of praise, either, but I did appreciate the sequence involving Akira, the goblin village chief, losing his temper and retaliating, Karen reprimanding him, and Akira subsequently reflecting on his actions.

Then again, wasn't the whole situation ridiculous from the start? Sending villagers on a business trip into territory where someone holds a grudge against you—and where killing monsters carries no legal consequences—without even providing an escort? What could possibly go wrong?

I don't dislike this series, but I can't say I particularly like it, either. I enjoy it reasonably well at times, but it's never something I actively look forward to watching. Maybe it's simply... easy to watch?
review.jp:
第6話: ː 衣類攻撃を仕掛けてみたけど質問ある?

"悪くはない、色気押しばかりの前回より遥かにマシ、気になる所もあるがそれ以上にまとも?だった"

『特に悪くはなかったかな・・・と。やり直しという異常レベルにチートな能力を持つ王子とのやり取りは、まぁ設定上の興味を惹くもの以外の意味ではある意味しらけるけど、悪くはなかった。ただ、明らかに風上に移動しているのでもうちょっと考察すべきだろうな…と感じてしまう。こういうのは、常にプロット優先、見せたいモノのためにすべてが動くものを見ている時に共通に感じる残念感でもある。それ以外も突出して褒め称えたいものもないけど、ゴブリン村長アキラのキレた報復とカレンの窘め、またそれで反省する流れなども悪くなかったと思う。っていうか、そもそも自分に恨みを持つものがいる所に、しかもモンスターなら殺しても罰せられない場所に村民を商売目的で送り込む、しかも護衛も付けない?は最初からおかしいでしょ?とは思う。嫌いじゃないけど好きでもないし、それなりに楽しんでる時もあるけど、楽しみにはしてない作品。見やすい…ってだけか?』－8話・視聴継続

review.en:
Episode #6: Each of Their Resolves

"What the hell was that?! They skip over everything in between, the story barely makes sense, and even the payoff is ridiculous... I think I'm about done with this show."

What on earth was that supposed to be? Apparently, we're just skipping everything that happens in between now. For reasons I couldn't quite follow, Romelia takes the twins into town to do some shopping. Then comes the painfully obvious setup: "Nobody but our mother can tell us apart..." I immediately had a bad feeling about where this was going.

On their way back, they're suddenly attacked by bandits—or whoever those guys were—and the next thing we know, they're tied up and being held captive. After various developments, Romelia manages to escape using a knife she'd apparently hidden on her, and she rescues the twins as well. But just when it looks like the bandits have discovered them and things are about to get ugly... surprise! The bandit leaders are twins, too. Okay, and?

Anyway, the entire squad suddenly shows up to rescue everyone, and just like that, everything is resolved. And the explanation for how Romelia can tell the twins apart? Apparently, it's because she once rode a pair of twin horses. Seriously? That's the big payoff? What a ridiculous ending. None of this makes any sense.
review.jp:
第6話: ː それぞれの覚悟

"なんじゃこりゃ~!途中も描かないし意味不明、オチもしょうもないし…、もう無理かなぁ。"

何じゃこりゃ?途中を一切描かないのね。よく分からんが双子を連れて街に買い物に。その双子の「お母さん以外誰も僕らを見分けてくれない・・・」という分かりやすい振りに不穏な兆しを感じる。帰りにいきなり盗賊?に襲われ、次の瞬間には縛られて味とに。まぁ色々あって、ロメリアは隠し持ってたナイフ?で脱出、双子も救ったが、盗賊にバレてまずいことに・・・と思ったら、盗賊のオカシラも双子…、で?いずれにしても部隊のみんながいきなり登場して助けてくれて一件落着。ロメリアが双子を見分けられるのは、かつて双子の馬に乗ってたことがあるから…とかいうしょうもないオチ。意味不明。

Facing overwhelming challenges—no army, no healers, no funds, and only inexperienced recruits—Romelia uses her wit and determination to turn the odds in her favor. She seizes fortresses from local lords to build her forces, negotiates with the church for healing, secures funds from merchants, and has her soldiers gain experience through monster hunting. Against all expectations, Romelia rises from the ashes, leading her loyal followers in a daring campaign to rescue her people and prove her worth.

Episode #6: ː RED AND BLUE, NIGHTS AND STARS

"Not a single aspect of this story interests me. I'm tired of Eleonora getting flustered and embarrassed, too. Can we please move things along already?"

I seriously can't bring myself to care. Not about the country that Mr. Can't-Sleep and Eleonora are visiting, not about the people apparently plotting something or the requests being made of them, and certainly not even about the two main characters themselves.

And we've spent something like three episodes now watching Eleonora, his childhood friend and fiancée, become increasingly conscious of her romantic feelings and get all flustered about them. Enough already. If something interesting doesn't happen next episode, I might just drop this show.

This time, Eleonora inexplicably goes to see some mysterious old guy at night. While they're talking, a bunch of soldiers suddenly show up and surround them. Just when it looks like things might get dangerous, Mr. Not-So-Sleepy somehow appears out of nowhere, puts everyone to sleep, and... problem solved.

Huh?? What was that supposed to be? Some kind of ridiculous farce?
review.jp:
第6話: ː 赤と青と夜と星と

"どの要素にもなんにも興味が持てない。エレオノーラの照れ、取り乱しにも飽きた、進めてくれ。"

マジで興味が持てない。眠れないくんとエレオノーラが訪れている国にも、何やら画策している連中、要請にも、ましてやメインの2人にさえ…。そしてこの幼馴染の許婚であるエレオノーラが、恋愛感情を意識しだして取り乱す、というクダリをこの3話くらいずっとやってる・・・。流石に飽きた。次になんか面白くないと切るかも。今回はエレオノーラが夜に謎のおっさんのいるところになぜか行って、話してたら兵士たちがゾロゾロ来て囲まれて、ヤバいかなと思ったらどこからともなく眠くないくんがいつの間にか来ていて、そいつらを眠らせてオーケー…。は?? これは何?茶番?ってことです。

entries.synopsis:
At the center of a continent made up of eight kingdoms lies the Kingdom of Marronnier. Leading the nation is the female general Baribara, who has seven sons, each with a personality all his own.

Sleepy, benevolent, sensitive to heat, sensitive to cold, gifted with animals, proud of his swordsmanship, and always hungry—the brothers possess very different qualities, but they are united by a single goal: "Someday, we'll rescue a princess in a cool way!"

Before long, the brothers set out for the seven neighboring kingdoms as ambassadors. What encounters, trials, and destinies await them in these unfamiliar lands?

Set in a medieval-inspired fantasy world, this tale of romance and adventure begins.

(Source: MAL News)

review.en:
Episode #5

Episode #5ː Conflict
"Is 'Conflict' supposed to refer to the inner turmoil of viewers who've somehow made it through five episodes of this show? Not since 'Magic Academy' have I been this utterly baffled..."

[The storytelling is an absolute disaster. What on earth is going on with the series composition? Noriko's feelings for Izark have suddenly skyrocketed, and she's somehow learned a whole lot of the language, too. Did I accidentally skip an episode or two? Apparently, quite a bit of time has passed, though the show does a terrible job of conveying it. And now they're hugging each other...?

Then Izark abruptly leaves Noriko without saying a word. Why? This sort of development is fairly typical of shojo manga, where the storytelling and presentation can somehow make it feel convincing. But simply reproducing it in anime without making the slightest effort to adapt how it's presented leaves viewers completely unable to follow what's happening.

After a string of outrageous incidents, Noriko suddenly gets harassed by some thugs, then somehow ends up falling and tumbling down onto a riverbank—or wherever that was. And wouldn't you know it, she just happens to run into a parent and child who've been instructed to look for her. Why a parent and child, anyway?

What the hell is this?? What is this show even trying to accomplish? It's astonishing how catastrophically bad the storytelling is.

Tomoyo Kurosawa... what on earth is happening here?]
review.jp:
第5話: ː 葛藤（かっとう）

"この作品を第5話まで見てしまっている視聴者の中の「葛藤」のこと?「魔法学園」以来の意味わかんねーよ…です"

絶望的な構成、シリーズ構成はどうなってる?1,2話くらい見忘れてた?って思うくらい唐突にノリコのイザークに対する想いは爆上がり、言葉も大分覚えてる…なんかよく分からない感じで時間が経過しているらしい。なんか抱き合ってるし・・・。で、唐突に何も言わずにイザークはノリコの元を去る。何故?こういったものは少女漫画特有で、マンガだとなんとなく納得の行く見せ方が出来るが、何の工夫も無くアニメでも同じ様に見せても誰も全くついてこれない。そして色々とんでもアプニングあってから、唐突に輩に絡まれるノリコ、そして河原?に落ちて転がってくるノリコ…。ノリコを探すように指示を受けていた親子（何故親子?）とたまたま出会う…。何だこれ??何がしたい?凄いなこれ、破滅的。黒沢ともよさん・・・何が起きている?

entries.synopsis:
Noriko Tachiki has dreamt of a beautiful fantasy land for some time, though her friends think it is only her imagination. One day, on her way home, Noriko stumbles upon a bomb disguised as a paper bag that explodes right in front of her. However, instead of dying, she is transported to a mysterious forest full of strange plants and creatures.

As she begins navigating through the woods, Noriko is suddenly attacked by a giant, worm-like monster. Fortunately, she is saved by Izark Kia Tarj, a swordsman who does not speak her language. Lacking the strength to survive on her own, Noriko decides to follow her stoic savior, taking the opportunity to learn the foreign land's language and be more useful to Izark.

Unbeknownst to her, Noriko is a crucial piece of an ancient prophecy. She is "The Awakening"—a being destined to unleash the greatest evil known as the "Sky Demon." With influential people plotting to capture Noriko for her supposed powers, both she and Izark must fend for themselves and overcome a future laced with chaos.

[Written by MAL Rewrite]
entries.synopsis_ja:
ごく普通の日々を送っていた女子高生・立木典子（たちき のりこ）は、ある朝見た不思議な夢に誘われるように、見知らぬ異世界へと迷い込んでしまう。言葉も常識も通用しないこの世界で、行く当てもなく彷徨う典子を救ったのは、たった一人で旅を続ける渡り戦士・イザークだった。
時を同じくして、世界中では「破壊をもたらす“天上鬼”を目覚めさせる者が現れる」「どの国よりも早く手に入れろ」と囁かれていた。目覚めとは、そして天上鬼とは何なのか——その答えを知るかのように、イザークは典子を見て呟く。
「この娘を殺さなければならない」言葉も文化も異なる二人の間には、それでも少しずつ小さな絆が芽生えていく。
そんな二人は、やがて壮大な運命の渦へと飲み込まれていく——。
